title: The One With All The Wedding Dresses

jokes.text: Opening shot: someone (presumably Chandler) reacting with 'Are you kidding me?' to Joey's snoring, followed by 'Joey?' — implying Joey is somehow snoring in another room loudly enough to wake him
jokes.setup: Cold open with no context — just an exasperated outburst
jokes.punchline: The name 'Joey' implies the audience already knows Joey snores and this is entirely his fault
jokes.explanation: Classic cold-open economy — two lines establish the entire conflict of the subplot. Works on character recognition (Joey = snorer is instantly believable) but isn't a crafted joke so much as a tease.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: So... nice weather we're having.

dialogue.speaker: Gunther
dialogue.line: You don't have to do that.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Do what?

dialogue.speaker: Gunther
dialogue.line: Fill the silence. It's okay. The silence is fine.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Oh. Okay...

jokes.text: Rachel to Gunther: 'You don't need to fill these silences.' Gunther: 'Okay, thanks.'
jokes.setup: Gunther is awkwardly trying to make conversation with Rachel
jokes.punchline: Rachel dismisses him bluntly, and Gunther responds with a genuinely grateful 'Okay, thanks' — relieved to be let off the hook rather than hurt
jokes.explanation: The 'Okay, thanks' is the entire joke — Gunther's relief at not having to perform romantically is funnier than any comeback could be. Tight, character-specific, and lands on a beat that feels very true to his personality. Good economy.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: There is no sleep clinic for that.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: What about the Institute for People Who Sleep With Their Eyes Open and Wake Up Screaming?

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: That's not a real thing.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Well, there should be!

jokes.text: Chandler: 'That's your fourth cup of coffee.' Joey: 'Okay, do me. I've had a certain number of juices.'
jokes.setup: Chandler is tracking coffee consumption as evidence of exhaustion; Joey wants to participate in the game
jokes.punchline: 'A certain number of juices' — Joey can't actually count how many juices he's had, which is both dim and self-aware
jokes.explanation: Joey's vague self-reporting ('a certain number') is a quintessential Joey line — lovably dumb, delivered with total sincerity. The joke earns its laugh through character specificity; only Joey would volunteer this admission.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: You could try sleeping on your side.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Oh, yeah!

jokes.text: Ross on Joey's snoring: 'He's in a different room. He's that loud?' Joey: 'You should hear me.'
jokes.setup: Ross is incredulous that snoring from another room is waking Chandler
jokes.punchline: Joey proudly confirms it — 'You should hear me' — with zero self-awareness that this is a problem
jokes.explanation: Joey's pride in his own disruptive snoring is a solid character beat. 'You should hear me' as a boast rather than an apology is the entire joke in four words.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I can't believe you're engaged!

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: What? Why not?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: No, no, it's not that... I mean, it's not because you're undateable or anything.

jokes.text: Joey invents the 'Quit-being-a-baby-and-leave-me-alone clinic' in response to being told to go to a sleep clinic
jokes.setup: Chandler tells Joey to go to a sleep clinic
jokes.punchline: Joey deflects by inventing a ridiculous counter-clinic: 'You should go to a Quit-being-a-baby-and-leave-me-alone clinic'
jokes.explanation: Classic Joey defensive logic — name a fake institution as a rhetorical escape hatch. The name itself is unwieldy in a funny way, and his delivery of 'They don't have those / Yeah, they do' is a great setup for the next beat.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Whoa, whoa, whoa! You are so whipped! *makes ridiculous sound effect*

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: What was that sound?

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: That's the sound of a whip!

jokes.text: Joey: 'They don't have those.' Chandler: 'Yeah, they do. Quit being a baby and leave me alone! There, you just had your first class.'
jokes.setup: Joey says the fake clinic doesn't exist
jokes.punchline: Chandler immediately performs the first 'class' of the fake clinic by yelling the clinic's name at Joey
jokes.explanation: This is sharp sitcom writing: Chandler takes Joey's absurd premise and immediately weaponizes it against him in the most literal, satisfying way. 'There, you just had your first class' is the punchline that makes the whole exchange worthwhile — perfect structure, great economy.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: What? That's the sound a whip makes!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: No, it's not. A whip sounds like 'crack,' not 'pshhew.'

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Dude, I've seen Indiana Jones. I know what a whip sounds like.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Joey, you literally just made a sound like a cat being launched into space.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: That's because I'm really good at it!

jokes.text: Monica tells the story of her ex-boyfriend rolling her over when she snored, and says 'Oh, yeah!' with evident pleasure at the memory
jokes.setup: Monica is describing a practical solution to snoring — an ex would roll her over
jokes.punchline: 'Oh, yeah!' — the memory is clearly not just utilitarian; she's reliving something romantic/physical, derailing her own anecdote
jokes.explanation: A solid mid-range joke — Monica's involuntary nostalgia breaks the practical conversation in a funny way. It's not especially original but it lands on a recognizable human moment.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Could we please stop with the whip sound?

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: No! It's the only way I can communicate with you anymore!

jokes.text: Chandler's reaction beat when Ross walks in wearing a suit — the group immediately turns to what's on TV: 'Oh, the Olympics!'
jokes.setup: Ross enters, apparently looking unusually put-together (implied by context)
jokes.punchline: The group deflects immediately to the Olympics rather than acknowledge Ross, suggesting either his appearance warrants mockery they're suppressing or the moment is intentionally awkward
jokes.explanation: This moment is hard to fully read without visuals. The 'Oh, the Olympics!' likely lands as a mild laugh from the audience recognizing the deflection, but as written it doesn't translate clearly to a strong comedic beat.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: You know, Rachel, I think it's great that you're putting yourself out there. Sure, your dating life is a complete disaster, and yes, every relationship you have ends in catastrophic failure, but... you just keep trying. And that's... that's really brave.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Why do you sound like you're reading me my last rites?

jokes.text: On Ross being engaged: 'Because it's so fast. Not because you're a loser.'
jokes.setup: Chandler (or Monica) says they can't believe Ross is engaged
jokes.punchline: The clarification — 'not because you're a loser' — is funnier than any insult would have been, implying the loser reading was Ross's first interpretation
jokes.explanation: The clarification joke is a well-worn but effectively executed form — the fact that Ross needs to be told it's NOT because he's a loser is a stealth insult. Good economy and structure. It's character-specific to how the group talks to Ross.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: We've been on four dates! Four! That's basically an engagement!

jokes.text: Ross asks where Rachel is; Monica says 'She's upstairs not doing the dishes.'
jokes.setup: Ross asks where Rachel is
jokes.punchline: Monica's answer reveals her own ongoing grievance with Rachel under the guise of answering the question
jokes.explanation: Monica describing Rachel's location via her failure to do chores is a compact, character-true moment. The phrasing 'not doing the dishes' as a location is clever.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Oh, so I should just 'be more careful'? Thanks Ross, that's so helpful. I'll just add that to my list of things to worry about between my job and my love life.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: You know what? 'Be more careful.' I'll have it embroidered on a pillow.

jokes.text: Monica: 'I won't do them this time. Even if they sit there until—' [beat] 'I'll do them when I get home.'
jokes.setup: Monica declares she won't do Rachel's dishes this time, with real conviction
jokes.punchline: She folds within the same sentence — the declaration collapses before it's even finished
jokes.explanation: Monica's compulsive cleanliness defeating her own principles is a core character trait, and this collapses it beautifully into about ten words. The speed of her capitulation is the joke. High character integration.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Oh my God, this dress is so beautiful!

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: You know, 50% of marriages end in divorce.

jokes.text: Chandler mimes being 'whipped' — 'Wah-pah!'
jokes.setup: Chandler teases Ross for running errands for his fiancée — picking up her wedding dress
jokes.punchline: Chandler's whip-crack gesture and sound ('Wah-pah!') as a commentary on Ross being under Emily's thumb
jokes.explanation: The 'wah-pah' whipped gesture is a broad, low-craft bit — it's the kind of joke that gets an easy audience laugh through physicality but has no particular wit. Functions well as setup for the superior payoff in the next beat.

dialogue.speaker: Store Employee
dialogue.line: You're going to make such a beautiful bride.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I know, right? I've already picked out my colors.

jokes.text: Joey makes the 'Wah-pah!' whip-crack gesture and sound when discussing Ross picking up Emily's wedding dress
jokes.setup: Joey accuses Ross of being whipped because Emily has him running errands
jokes.punchline: Joey delivers a theatrical 'Wah-pah!' (whip sound) with an accompanying gesture — over-the-top physical comedy to emphasize 'whipped'
jokes.explanation: The 'wah-pah' joke is a staple of early-2000s sitcom humor — it's functional but not particularly creative. Gets a laugh primarily from the physical delivery.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Joey, you have to do something about your snoring. It's unbearable.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: What do you want me to do?

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I don't know! See a doctor, get surgery, go to a sleep clinic, visit the pajama store — something!

jokes.text: Ross says 'That's not whipped. Whipped is—' and then demonstrates the actual whipped gesture/sound himself, inadvertently proving Chandler's point
jokes.setup: Ross protests that he's not whipped and offers to demonstrate what 'whipped' actually looks like
jokes.punchline: His demonstration of 'whipped' is indistinguishable from Chandler's, confirming he is in fact whipped; the visual joke is that he's doing the exact thing he's arguing against
jokes.explanation: Ross disproving his own argument by illustrating it perfectly is a classic sitcom structural move. Works especially well as a visual gag — the audience sees him perform the exact motion he's trying to distinguish himself from. Good callback escalation.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Weddings are great for meeting women.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Yeah, that's why I'm always the first one on the dance floor.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Chandler, you're the last one on the dance floor. And usually security has to ask you to leave.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Well, at least I'm memorable.

jokes.text: Joey: 'You can't do anything!' — reacting to Ross's failed attempt to demonstrate he's not whipped
jokes.setup: Ross has just inadvertently demonstrated being whipped while trying to prove he isn't
jokes.punchline: Joey's gleeful condemnation caps the sequence with maximum simplicity
jokes.explanation: A capper line that works on simplicity. Joey's 'You can't do anything!' is the pile-on the audience expects; it earns its laugh by being exactly what the moment needs.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I can't dance. I have no rhythm, no coordination, nothing.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Watch this.

jokes.text: Rachel: 'Do you have a minute?' Monica: 'I was just about to take a break anyway.' — Monica is visibly not doing anything
jokes.setup: Rachel asks if Monica has a minute
jokes.punchline: Monica says she was 'just about to take a break anyway' despite apparently doing nothing
jokes.explanation: A mild, functional transitional joke. Gets a small laugh from the incongruity but doesn't have strong craft behind it.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: The wedding is in one month.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Oh my God, that's like... that's like my cycle!

jokes.text: Ross tells Rachel she just needs to 'hang in there' regarding finding love — condescending given she's been dating Joshua
jokes.setup: Ross is trying to be supportive of Rachel while obliviously unaware of her feelings about his engagement
jokes.punchline: 'You just hang in there' — catastrophically patronizing advice from her ex, delivered with utter sincerity
jokes.explanation: Ross's oblivious condescension is a cringe-comedy goldmine. 'Hang in there' to your ex who still has feelings for you — delivered as genuine kindness — is painfully well-observed. The setup is rich and the payoff lands on character truth.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I've been thinking about us, and I want to be more impulsive and crazy. You know, shake things up a little.

dialogue.speaker: Joshua
dialogue.line: Impulsive and crazy? Rachel, that's not really what I'm looking for in a relationship.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: But don't you want someone who keeps you on your toes? Someone spontaneous and exciting?

dialogue.speaker: Joshua
dialogue.line: I want someone stable. Someone I can count on.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Well, I'm going to be spontaneous starting right now. I'm going to dye my hair green!

dialogue.speaker: Joshua
dialogue.line: Please don't.

jokes.text: Rachel's desperate competitive move: 'I'm right there with Joshua. You are right there with Emily. And it's kind of like it's a tie.'
jokes.setup: Rachel is trying to convince Ross (and herself) that her relationship with Joshua is as serious as his with Emily
jokes.punchline: 'It's kind of like it's a tie' — an absurdly weak framing that reveals Rachel's desperation; relationships aren't competitions, and even if they were, 'a tie' isn't winning
jokes.explanation: This is the best joke of the Ross-Rachel scene — 'it's kind of like it's a tie' is tragicomically delusional. It works on multiple levels: it's funny as written, it's devastating as characterization, and it perfectly captures Rachel's psychological state. High character integration.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I want to be more spontaneous in our relationship.

dialogue.speaker: Joshua
dialogue.line: That's great.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: So... when are we getting married?

jokes.text: Both Ross and Rachel simultaneously invent urgent reasons to leave the deeply uncomfortable conversation
jokes.setup: The conversation has reached maximum emotional awkwardness with Rachel's 'tie' comment
jokes.punchline: Both characters immediately manufacture excuses to flee — 'I gotta get back to my dishes' / 'I gotta get to work'
jokes.explanation: The mutual escape is a structurally sound beat — both characters fleeing simultaneously confirms they both know the conversation has gone sideways. Functions well as a scene-ender.

dialogue.speaker: Joshua
dialogue.line: Rachel, I... wow. This is... I'm really flattered, but I think maybe we should pump the brakes here a little bit.

dialogue.speaker: Joshua
dialogue.line: I mean, we've been on four dates. Four! That's... that's not a lot of dates.

dialogue.speaker: Joshua
dialogue.line: And I like you, I do, but marriage is a big thing. It's like... it's like buying a house without seeing it first.

dialogue.speaker: Joshua
dialogue.line: Except the house is my life, and you're trying to move in after four viewings.

dialogue.speaker: Joshua
dialogue.line: So... maybe we could just, you know, date for a while? See where this goes?

jokes.text: Rachel mutters 'Hang in there. You hang in there.' under her breath and claims she's 'just singing' when asked
jokes.setup: Rachel is seething about Ross's condescending advice
jokes.punchline: She's so consumed by it she's literally muttering it to herself, then covers with 'just singing' — implying 'Hang in There' is somehow a song
jokes.explanation: A satisfying callback that deepens the comedic humiliation. Rachel can't let it go, which is both funny and revealing. 'Just singing' is a perfect cover-up line.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Oh my God, what did I just do?

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I just proposed to him! I proposed to him! Who does that?!

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: I'm an idiot. I'm such an idiot.

jokes.text: Monica, surrounded by brides: 'About half of these will end up getting divorced.'
jokes.setup: Monica and Rachel are surrounded by excited brides in the shop
jokes.punchline: Monica's statistic-based cynicism in the most inappropriate possible setting — delivered flatly amid all the joy
jokes.explanation: Perfect comic timing and economy — one flat sentence that cuts against the entire emotional register of the scene. The deadpan delivery in a room full of bridal joy is exactly right. High quotability, slightly dark, efficiently executed.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Well, I'm a heavy sleeper, so I wouldn't hear it anyway. But I'm willing to stay up all night just to hear you say something interesting.

jokes.text: The shop assistant asks 'Would you like to try it on, Miss Waltham?' — addressing Monica or Rachel as 'Miss Waltham' (Emily's name), and they go along with it
jokes.setup: Monica or Rachel is picking up a dress for Emily — they're not the bride
jokes.punchline: The assistant invites 'Miss Waltham' to try it on, and one of them accepts the identity — the whole dress-trying sequence follows from this mistaken identity
jokes.explanation: The setup for a classic 'we shouldn't be doing this' bit. The joke is in the temptation and the ease with which they slip into it. Functional rather than exceptional.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Oh, I'm sorry, I didn't realize we were going for realism in our fantasy game!

jokes.text: Rachel (in the wedding dress): 'You're the most beautiful bride I've ever seen.' Monica (in the dress): 'I am, aren't I?'
jokes.setup: Monica is wearing someone else's wedding dress, which she shouldn't be doing
jokes.punchline: 'I am, aren't I?' — Monica's utter unselfconsciousness; she accepts the compliment with total sincerity, her competitive vanity taking over
jokes.explanation: Monica's total self-assurance in a dress that isn't hers, responding to a rhetorical compliment with earnest agreement, is pitch-perfect character comedy. 'I am, aren't I?' has the right amount of weight — she's not joking, and that makes it funnier.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Oh my God, we're grown women playing with wedding dresses.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: I know. It's pretty pathetic.

jokes.text: Shop assistant informs them they're closing; Rachel/Monica have been in the dresses long enough to need to be kicked out
jokes.setup: Monica and Rachel got swept up trying on wedding dresses
jokes.punchline: The shop is closing — they've been in the dresses so long the shop is literally shutting down around them
jokes.explanation: The escalation is implied and funny — time has passed to the point of absurdity. Works as a beat but isn't a crafted joke in its own right.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: This isn't even my dress.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Where'd you get it?

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I borrowed it from my friend.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Well, I got mine at a store called 'Suck It Up.'

jokes.text: Shop assistant: 'And could I get my ring back?' — Monica or Rachel has been wearing the shop's display ring this whole time
jokes.setup: Monica and Rachel are being ushered out of the shop after spending too long in wedding dresses
jokes.punchline: They've gone so deep into the fantasy that someone has taken the shop's engagement ring — the assistant has to ask for it back
jokes.explanation: This is the best single joke in the bridal shop scene. 'Could I get my ring back?' reframes the whole sequence retroactively — they haven't just tried on dresses, they've fully committed to the fantasy including accessories. The ask is so mundane against such absurdity that it lands perfectly. Good economy, genuine surprise.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I'm not changing out of this dress.

jokes.text: Chandler sneaking into Joey's room to roll him over — 'All right, buddy. Time to roll over.' — followed by the horror of what he encounters
jokes.setup: Chandler has decided to implement Monica's ex-boyfriend's snoring solution: rolling Joey over
jokes.punchline: The sheer absurdity of Chandler sneaking into Joey's room in the dark to physically roll his grown male roommate over in bed
jokes.explanation: A solid callback payoff to the earlier snoring solution discussion. The absurdity is in the domestic intimacy of the act — this is not what the solution was designed for, but Chandler has committed.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I can't wear regular clothes anymore. This dress has ruined me for everything else.

jokes.text: Chandler, apparently traumatized by what he encountered: 'You are going to a clinic! You're going to a clinic!'
jokes.setup: Chandler went in to roll Joey over and apparently discovered something far worse than expected
jokes.punchline: His reaction has escalated dramatically — he's now screaming the original demand with new conviction, implying the experience was deeply disturbing
jokes.explanation: The escalation works well because we don't know exactly what Chandler saw — the specificity of his trauma is left to the imagination, which is funnier. Good callback to the clinic demand.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: How did you get the girl instead of Joey?

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: Well, Joey was literally unconscious.

jokes.text: Chandler adds: 'And a pajama store!'
jokes.setup: Chandler has just declared Joey must go to a clinic
jokes.punchline: The addition of 'and a pajama store' implies Joey was sleeping in something (or nothing) deeply inappropriate — a one-line joke that fires entirely on implication
jokes.explanation: This is one of the episode's best lines. 'And a pajama store!' works entirely through implication — the audience fills in what Chandler must have seen, and whatever they imagine is funnier than any explicit description. Perfect economy (four words), great escalation structure, and the absurdity of 'pajama store' as a prescription is inspired. Genuinely clever writing.

dialogue.speaker: Joey
dialogue.line: Hey, you know what? This anti-snoring device tastes like a hockey puck, but at least I'm not snoring anymore.

jokes.text: Monica doing the dishes while counting each item: 'Does she use the cups? Yes, I believe she does. Does she use the plates? Yes, I believe she does!'
jokes.setup: Monica has surrendered to doing Rachel's dishes despite vowing not to
jokes.punchline: She's narrating her own grievance aloud, treating the discovery of each dirty dish as evidence in a trial against Rachel
jokes.explanation: Monica's self-righteous narration while doing the very thing she swore not to do is excellent character comedy. The rhetorical-question format ('Does she use the cups? Yes, I believe she does') gives it an almost legal formality that makes it funnier. Strong character integration — this is quintessential Monica.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Joshua, hi, it's me. I just wanted to call and tell you that I'm not crazy. I know what I did was impulsive, but I'm not crazy. I just... I really like you, and I thought maybe we could talk about this. So... call me back, okay?

dialogue.speaker: Answering Machine
dialogue.line: [beep]

jokes.text: Joey complaining about having to stay up all night before the sleep clinic: 'This sucks. I have to stay up all night before I go to the stupid clinic. I'm so tired.' Chandler: 'It's six o'clock.'
jokes.setup: Joey is complaining about staying up all night for the sleep study
jokes.punchline: It's only 6 PM — Joey's endurance complaint is hilariously premature
jokes.explanation: Classic Joey joke structure: he makes a complaint that sounds reasonable, then Chandler reveals it's completely unwarranted. 'It's six o'clock' is the perfect, economical punchline. This format works every time with these characters.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Make dinner reservations for three.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Three? That's pretty late. Most restaurants stop serving at two.

jokes.text: Rachel's confident prediction that Ross and Emily's engagement will collapse: 'They'll be engaged for like what? A year? One of them will realize what they've done and call it off.'
jokes.setup: Rachel is reassuring herself (and Phoebe or Monica) that she's fine with Ross's engagement
jokes.punchline: Her 'rational' prediction is transparently wishful thinking — delivered with absolute confidence, which makes it both funny and sad
jokes.explanation: Rachel's rationalization that the engagement will fail is painfully transparent. The specificity ('like what, a year?') makes it funnier — she's already done the math on how long she has to wait. Good dramatic irony for a rewatch audience.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Why did Joshua break up with you?

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Well, I may have accidentally proposed to him.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: You proposed to him?

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: He didn't take it well.

jokes.text: Rachel: 'You'll be dancing at my wedding before you dance at theirs.' Chandler/Joey: 'You know, I don't dance at weddings.'
jokes.setup: Rachel triumphantly declares she'll be married before Ross and Emily
jokes.punchline: Instead of engaging with her declaration, the response is a mundane logistical correction — 'I don't dance at weddings' — completely deflating her dramatic moment
jokes.explanation: Classic deflation joke — Rachel's big romantic declaration is immediately brought down to earth by a practical non-sequitur. The mismatch in registers (epic vs. mundane) is the whole joke.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: Are you going to be okay?

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Yeah, I'll be fine. I have Monica, Phoebe, and you guys.

dialogue.speaker: Ross
dialogue.line: That's great, Rach.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Besides, who needs a man when you have friends like these?

jokes.text: On why he doesn't dance at weddings: 'Weddings are a great place to meet women. When I dance, I look like this.' — followed by a presumably hideous dance demonstration
jokes.setup: Asked why he doesn't dance at weddings when they're a great place to meet women
jokes.punchline: His dancing is so bad it would actively harm his prospects — the demonstration is the punchline
jokes.explanation: Physical comedy bit that works on the contrast: Chandler is strategic about not dancing (weddings = meeting women) but his dancing is bad enough to negate all strategy. The unseen demonstration is funnier than whatever it actually is.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I wish I could wear a wedding dress to work.

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Oh, you could be a wedding dress model!

jokes.text: Ross tells the gang the wedding is in a month — 'Because we're getting married in a month.'
jokes.setup: Ross asked what the guys are doing in four weeks
jokes.punchline: He announces the wedding is in a MONTH — shocking escalation of the timeline
jokes.explanation: The reveal lands on the audience's disbelief and the gang's reactions. Functions as an escalation of the 'rushed engagement' theme.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Oh my God, Chandler! You can't see us! It's bad luck!

dialogue.speaker: Phoebe
dialogue.line: Yeah, groom can't see the bride before the wedding!

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: You're not actually getting married.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: I don't care! The universe doesn't know that!

jokes.text: Chandler's baffled processing of the timeline: 'What? ... In a month? ... You mean 30 days? ... From now?'
jokes.setup: Ross announces the wedding is in a month
jokes.punchline: Chandler breaks down the same information into progressively more specific restatements, as if each version might be less true than the last
jokes.explanation: Chandler's escalating restatements ('a month... you mean 30 days... from now?') are a great comedic beat — each question is technically redundant but emotionally necessary, as if the truth might change. This is very Chandler-specific: his comic mode is baffled disbelief expressed in increasingly precise terms.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: If Chandler sees me in this dress before the wedding, he'll break up with me.

dialogue.speaker: Rachel
dialogue.line: Monica, that's not how it works.

dialogue.speaker: Monica
dialogue.line: Oh really? Because I'm pretty sure if he sees me looking this good, he'll realize he can do better.

jokes.text: Joey, after Ross explains the rushed timeline: 'Hey, that's the day after I start menstruating!'
jokes.setup: Ross explains the wedding is in a month because the venue is being torn down
jokes.punchline: Joey contributes this scheduling conflict — apparently tracking his cycle with complete sincerity
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's best lines. The genius is total commitment — Joey isn't making a joke, he's raising a genuine scheduling concern. The gap between the gravity of the situation (wedding logistics) and Joey's concern (his menstrual cycle, delivered as a plain fact) is enormous. 'The day after I start menstruating' is specific in a way that's funnier than any vague absurdism would be. High quotability, iconic Joey moment.

dialogue.speaker: Chandler
dialogue.line: I just want to say, when I picture my wedding day, I always imagined Monica and Phoebe screaming at me like this.

jokes.text: Rachel's desperate insistence to Joshua that they're 'clicking' and 'working' — 'I think we are so on the right track.'
jokes.setup: Rachel is trying to convince Joshua (and herself) that everything is great
jokes.punchline: The sheer volume of her reassurance — 'clicking,' 'working,' 'right track' — is inversely proportional to how true it is; she's protesting too much
jokes.explanation: Classic cringe setup — the audience can see the disaster coming before Rachel can. Her over-enthusiasm is the tell. Functional cringe comedy but not particularly original.

jokes.text: Rachel says they need to be 'crazy' — Joshua hopefully interprets this as: 'Are you gonna put on that cheerleader outfit again?'
jokes.setup: Rachel says their relationship needs to be 'more crazy'
jokes.punchline: Joshua immediately interprets 'crazy' as a reference to a cheerleader outfit — both a window into their actual relationship and a way to tell us (without telling us) what their physical dynamic is like
jokes.explanation: A well-constructed implication joke — we learn more about Rachel and Joshua's relationship through one offhand question than any direct exposition. The cheerleader outfit reveals he's interested in the relationship and that they've had fun, which makes Rachel's proposal even sadder.

jokes.text: Rachel proposes marriage to Joshua after four dates
jokes.setup: Rachel has been building to asking Joshua to 'go crazy' with her
jokes.punchline: 'What if we got married?' — the most catastrophic possible interpretation of 'crazy,' delivered after four dates
jokes.explanation: The pivot to a marriage proposal after four dates is the comedic climax of Rachel's entire arc this episode. It's both hilarious and painful — she's so desperate to prove she's as far along as Ross and Emily that she detonates the relationship. The character motivation is entirely coherent, which makes it both funnier and sadder.

jokes.text: Joshua's rejection speech: 'Rachel...you're...a real...special lady. But my divorce isn't final yet...and we've been on four dates. So I'm thinking: No...but...thanks.'
jokes.setup: Rachel has just proposed marriage after four dates
jokes.punchline: 'No...but...thanks.' — the politest, most excruciating rejection speech, delivered with agonizing pauses; the 'but...thanks' is the perfect button
jokes.explanation: Joshua's rejection is a masterwork of cringe comedy construction. Each element is perfect: 'a real special lady' (damning with faint praise), the enumerated reasons (divorce not final + four dates), and 'No...but...thanks' — especially the 'but' before 'thanks,' which creates a beat of false hope before confirming the no. The ellipses are load-bearing comedy. One of the episode's best crafted moments.

jokes.text: Rachel, after Joshua leaves: 'You idiot!'
jokes.setup: Joshua has just delivered his polite rejection and left
jokes.punchline: Rachel's self-condemnation — 'You idiot!' — the audience has been waiting for her to realize this and the speed of self-awareness is satisfying
jokes.explanation: Perfect button on the Joshua scene. 'You idiot!' is exactly what every viewer is thinking, and Rachel saying it herself transforms the cringe into catharsis. Economy: two words, maximum effect.

jokes.text: Joey at the sleep clinic, checking out a woman: 'Check out that girl. She's really hot.'
jokes.setup: Joey and Chandler are in the waiting room of a sleep clinic
jokes.punchline: Joey's first instinct in any situation is to check out women — including at a medical facility where everyone is there for a disorder
jokes.explanation: Classic Joey beat — the character's libido transcends any context. Functional but not especially crafted; it's Joey being Joey in a new location.

jokes.text: Joey attempting his 'How you doing?' pickup line on the entire sleep clinic waiting room
jokes.setup: Joey spots an attractive woman at the sleep clinic
jokes.punchline: He delivers 'How you doing?' not to her specifically but apparently to the whole room — a visual gag where his signature line misfires in scale
jokes.explanation: The 'How you doing?' running gag lands differently when it's directed at an entire room rather than one person. Chandler's correction ('You're coming on to the entire room') reframes it perfectly. High character integration — this is Joey's signature bit executed with a twist.

jokes.text: Chandler: 'You're coming on to the entire room.'
jokes.setup: Joey has apparently directed his flirtation at the whole waiting room
jokes.punchline: Chandler's flat, matter-of-fact observation — not outrage, just factual correction
jokes.explanation: Classic Chandler straight-man line. The economy is what makes it — he could have said much more, but the flat statement of the problem is funnier than any elaboration.

jokes.text: Chandler's sleep clinic pickup: 'I'm Chandler.' 'I'm Marjorie.' 'So what are you in for? I talk in my sleep.' 'What a coincidence! I listen in my sleep.'
jokes.setup: Chandler meets an attractive woman at the sleep clinic — she reveals she talks in her sleep
jokes.punchline: 'What a coincidence! I listen in my sleep.' — Chandler reframes his condition (presumably insomnia from snoring) as a compatible quality, transforming a disability into a romantic asset
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's best-crafted jokes. 'I listen in my sleep' is an inspired reframe — it takes Chandler's sleep problem and converts it into a romantic compatibility through pure rhetorical sleight of hand. It's also a believable Chandler move: he's the character who uses wit to compensate. The structure (her confession → his logical mirror response) is tight and the punchline arrives exactly on time. Very quotable.

jokes.text: Chandler gets called in for his study right after getting the number — 'I got it! Mine!'
jokes.setup: Joey was also trying to pick up Marjorie; Chandler succeeded
jokes.punchline: The nurse calls Chandler's name at the exact moment of his victory — triumphing over Joey at the last second
jokes.explanation: Light victory moment, works as a beat. The timing of the nurse's call adds to the comedy but isn't especially crafted.

jokes.text: Monica and Rachel in wedding dresses throwing the bouquet to each other — 'My turn, my turn! Okay, ready?'
jokes.setup: Monica and Rachel are still in the wedding dresses at the apartment — the escape from the shop didn't stop the fantasy
jokes.punchline: They're throwing the bouquet to each other, enacting a wedding ritual for themselves
jokes.explanation: The escalation of the dress subplot — they've brought it home and are now doing full wedding rituals alone. The visual image of two friends in wedding dresses throwing a bouquet to each other in an apartment is inherently funny and gains resonance from the emotional context.

jokes.text: Rachel: 'That was a terrible throw!' Monica: 'I won't throw it right to you. That's not real.'
jokes.setup: Rachel complains about Monica's bouquet throw
jokes.punchline: Monica insists on the realistic integrity of a fake wedding ritual she's conducting alone with her friend — 'That's not real' — Monica's competitive perfectionism applied to something inherently absurd
jokes.explanation: Monica refusing to throw the bouquet 'right to her' because 'that's not real' is a great character joke. She's so committed to the ritual's authenticity that she's imposing real rules on a wholly imaginary scenario. The character integration is excellent — only Monica would care about the competitive integrity of an imaginary bouquet toss.

jokes.text: Rachel: 'Look at me. My big concern is what's real?'
jokes.setup: Rachel has just complained about the realism of a bouquet toss in a fake wedding
jokes.punchline: Rachel's self-aware observation that she's also fully bought into the fantasy — 'My big concern is what's real?' — is both funny and loaded with emotional resonance
jokes.explanation: Rachel's self-awareness arrives a beat too late — she's already invested in the fantasy before realizing she's invested in the fantasy. The line functions simultaneously as self-deprecating humor and genuine emotional honesty, which is the best kind of sitcom writing.

jokes.text: Monica: 'Oh, my God! We're really sad, aren't we?'
jokes.setup: Monica and Rachel have been throwing bouquets to each other in wedding dresses
jokes.punchline: Monica suddenly sees the full picture of what they're doing — 'We're really sad, aren't we?' — the fourth-wall-adjacent moment of self-recognition
jokes.explanation: A satisfying acknowledgment of the absurdity — works as a release valve after the mounting weirdness of the dress sequence. Good economy.

jokes.text: Rachel: 'Yeah, I think we are. This isn't even my dress.' Monica: 'At least you didn't rent yours from a store called "It's Not Too Late."'
jokes.setup: Monica and Rachel are acknowledging they're sad women in wedding dresses in an apartment
jokes.punchline: 'At least you didn't rent yours from a store called It's Not Too Late' — Monica has apparently rented a wedding dress from a store with an aggressively desperate name, implying she did this before or regularly
jokes.explanation: The best joke in the episode. 'It's Not Too Late' as a store name is inspired — it's both a business name and an existential plea. The fact that Monica has apparently rented a dress from this store (implying this isn't her first time doing this) is devastating and hilarious in equal measure. The name is brilliantly specific, the dark subtext is rich, and the delivery is effortlessly confident. This is the kind of joke you remember years later. High originality, perfect economy, strong character integration (Monica's marriage anxiety is her defining trait).

jokes.text: They start throwing the bouquet again: 'All right, now throw it straight this time.' Rachel catches and screams: 'I'm getting married!'
jokes.setup: Monica and Rachel have decided to continue in the dresses for another half hour
jokes.punchline: Rachel catching the bouquet and screaming 'I'm getting married!' — the delusion is now total; she's fully in the fantasy
jokes.explanation: 'I'm getting married!' as a genuine emotional peak of a wholly imaginary scenario is funny and heartbreaking simultaneously. The escalation from 'we're sad' to full delusion in the span of one bouquet catch is well-paced.

jokes.text: Rachel: 'I hate my regular clothes now.'
jokes.setup: Rachel is fully immersed in the wedding dress fantasy
jokes.punchline: The completely mundane, petulant complaint — 'I hate my regular clothes now' — reduces the existential wedding anxiety to the level of a wardrobe preference
jokes.explanation: One of the best lines of the episode. 'I hate my regular clothes now' is disarmingly simple but captures the entire emotional landscape — the dress as an avatar for the life Rachel wants but doesn't have. It's both genuinely funny and unexpectedly moving. Maximum economy, strong character integration, and highly quotable.

jokes.text: Phoebe to Monica/Rachel: 'Oh, my God! You're such a cheater!' — apparently catching them in the dress game
jokes.setup: Phoebe arrives to find Monica and Rachel doing something with the dresses
jokes.punchline: 'You're such a cheater!' — Phoebe treats it as a game violation, not as the deeply sad ritual it is; her oblivious framing is funny
jokes.explanation: Phoebe's arrival and her immediate accusation of cheating (rather than questioning why they're in dresses) is a character-appropriate beat. Mild laugh.

jokes.text: Chandler's claim to have beaten Joey to the girl: 'Joey wanted to ask her out, but, you know, she picked me.' Joey: 'How'd that happen?' Chandler: 'Because I'm cooler.' Joey: 'No, seriously.'
jokes.setup: Chandler brags that the girl from the sleep clinic chose him over Joey
jokes.punchline: 'Because I'm cooler.' Joey: 'No, seriously.' — Joey's immediate, sincere dismissal of the possibility that Chandler is cooler than him
jokes.explanation: Joey's 'No, seriously' is the punchline — he doesn't even consider 'because I'm cooler' as a possible answer. The two-step (Chandler's answer → Joey's straight-faced dismissal) is well-timed and character-specific.

jokes.text: Chandler's actual explanation for beating Joey: 'She's the kind of girl... Joey was unconscious.'
jokes.setup: Joey has asked how Chandler got the girl's number when Joey normally wins these contests
jokes.punchline: Chandler starts to give an answer about what kind of girl she is, then pivots to the real reason: Joey was asleep during the study. The partial sentence and pivot is the structure.
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's best-structured jokes. The abandoned sentence ('She's the kind of girl...') sets up an expectation of a compliment or character description, then the pivot to 'Joey was unconscious' reframes the entire situation. Chandler didn't win — the competition was simply suspended. Perfectly economical, great structure, and character-specific.

jokes.text: Joey returns from the sleep clinic wearing a CPAP mask: 'They gave it to me at the sleep clinic... and it's going to help me not to snore.'
jokes.setup: Joey has been to the sleep clinic to solve his snoring
jokes.punchline: He returns wearing a large, presumably terrifying CPAP/oxygen mask — the visual is the punchline
jokes.explanation: The visual payoff of the mask is the main joke here — the transcript can only gesture at it. The subsequent dialogue builds on the sight gag.

jokes.text: Everyone's reaction to Joey's sleep mask: 'Oh, my God! What is that?'
jokes.setup: Joey walks in with the sleep mask
jokes.punchline: The group's collective horror at the sight of whatever Joey is wearing
jokes.explanation: Classic reaction beat — the audience response mirrors the characters' horror. Limited craft on paper but the visual must be strong.

jokes.text: Joey, about the sleep mask: 'Well, are you asleep right now, Joe? You don't have to wear it unless you are.' Joey: 'I know I don't have to. It tastes good.'
jokes.setup: Chandler points out Joey doesn't have to wear the mask unless he's asleep
jokes.punchline: 'I know I don't have to. It tastes good.' — Joey is wearing a medical device recreationally because he likes the taste
jokes.explanation: Exceptional Joey joke. 'It tastes good' is an inspired reason to wear a sleep apnea mask while awake — only Joey would evaluate medical equipment on flavor. The delivery must be completely sincere for this to land (and it always does). High originality, perfect economy, strong character integration. This is very close to the calibration anchor level.

jokes.text: Chandler, after Joey's taste explanation: 'Plus, you look cool.'
jokes.setup: Joey has just said the sleep mask 'tastes good'
jokes.punchline: Chandler's flat addition of 'Plus, you look cool' — maximum sarcasm, delivered as a sincere compliment
jokes.explanation: 'Plus, you look cool' is the perfect button to the mask sequence — Chandler's deadpan sarcasm delivered as apparent sincerity. Four words, maximal comedy. His straight-man affirmation of Joey's delusion is funnier than any direct mockery would be.

jokes.text: Ross: 'Hope I didn't stretch Emily's dress.' Monica: 'Your butt's not that much bigger than hers.'
jokes.setup: Ross apparently tried on or held Emily's wedding dress (the one from the shop)
jokes.punchline: Monica's 'your butt's not that much bigger than hers' — a mild insult dressed as reassurance, implying Ross's butt IS bigger but not catastrophically so
jokes.explanation: A reliable body joke with the gentle savagery that characterizes Friends dialogue. 'Not that much bigger' is the operative phrase — the qualification makes it both reassurance and insult. Solid.

jokes.text: Rachel on her attempt to convince Joshua she's not crazy: 'His answering machine was very understanding.'
jokes.setup: Monica asks how Rachel's call to Joshua went
jokes.punchline: 'His answering machine was very understanding' — she didn't reach him; she left a message on a machine that she's characterizing as emotionally responsive
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's best lines. 'His answering machine was very understanding' is densely packed: it reveals she didn't reach him (pathetic), that she left a message (more pathetic), and that she's attributing emotional intelligence to a machine (most pathetic). The word 'understanding' is doing enormous work. Perfect economy, strong character integration, very quotable. Comparable to the calibration anchors.

jokes.text: Rachel: 'I did my best to convince him that I'm not some crazy girl who's dying to get married... What'd he say? His answering machine was very understanding.'
jokes.setup: Rachel says she called Joshua to convince him she's not desperately wanting to get married
jokes.punchline: 'His answering machine was very understanding' — she left a message on his answering machine, didn't even reach him, and is treating the machine's passivity as a form of understanding
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's best lines. 'His answering machine was very understanding' is brilliantly structured — it takes a beat to land as the audience realizes she talked to a machine, not Joshua. The deadpan framing of an answering machine as an empathetic listener is both funny and painfully sad. It perfectly captures Rachel's humiliation and desperation. High quotability — this is a memorable Friends line. Close to the 8.0 anchor in quality.

jokes.text: Rachel's admission about Ross: 'I guess I just figured, somewhere down the road...we would be on again. Again.' Monica: 'You know what? I think we all did.'
jokes.setup: Rachel is admitting she's not okay with Ross's engagement because she still had hope
jokes.punchline: 'I think we all did' — Monica confirms the whole friend group has been waiting for Ross and Rachel to get back together, which is both validating and funny in its communal obviousness
jokes.explanation: Monica's 'I think we all did' is both funny (the friends have been following the Ross-Rachel will-they-won't-they with investment) and genuinely sweet. It earns a knowing laugh from the audience who also expected this.

jokes.text: Ross: 'Well, you'd better make it for three.' Rachel: '...I don't know if we're going to be hungry at three.' Ross: 'Three people. Joshua's not going to be there.'
jokes.setup: Ross is making restaurant reservations for a double date, saying 'make it for three'
jokes.punchline: Rachel mishears 'three' as the time (3 PM) rather than the number of people — the clarification lands the bad news (Joshua is gone) in the most matter-of-fact way
jokes.explanation: Classic misdirection setup — 'for three' reads as time before number. The clarification lands the Joshua revelation in a way that is both explanatory and awkward. Well-structured, good economy.

jokes.text: On why Joshua won't be at dinner: 'Well, I think he broke up with me.' Ross: 'No. Why?' Rachel: 'Apparently, he scares easy.'
jokes.setup: Ross asks why Joshua isn't coming to dinner
jokes.punchline: 'Apparently, he scares easy' — Rachel's flat, knowing understatement of the fact that she proposed marriage after four dates and he fled; 'scares easy' reframes her catastrophic behavior as his personality flaw
jokes.explanation: One of the episode's best lines. 'He scares easy' is a masterful deflection — it reattributes her entirely self-inflicted disaster to a character weakness in Joshua. The deadpan delivery of a catastrophically self-serving interpretation is pitch-perfect Rachel. Extremely quotable, great economy, strong character integration.

jokes.text: Ross about to leave, checking in: 'Are you okay?' Rachel: 'Yeah. I got my girls.'
jokes.setup: Ross is about to leave to pick up Emily; Rachel is sad about Joshua
jokes.punchline: The camera presumably reveals Monica and Rachel are still in the wedding dresses when she says 'I got my girls' — the word 'girls' in conjunction with two grown women in wedding dresses is the visual joke
jokes.explanation: The visual callback to the dresses is implied by the transcript — Ross's reaction to seeing them presumably in the dresses while Rachel says 'I got my girls' is both sweet and absurd. Works well as an emotional and comedic beat simultaneously.

jokes.text: Monica or Phoebe suggests something to cheer Rachel up — visual reveal that they're all three now in wedding dresses
jokes.setup: Monica or Phoebe suggests something to cheer Rachel up
jokes.punchline: The 'something' is putting on wedding dresses — Phoebe has joined the club; all three friends are now in wedding dresses together in the apartment
jokes.explanation: The escalation of the dress gag reaching its peak — three friends in wedding dresses is significantly funnier than two, and the audience's anticipation of what the 'cheer-up' suggestion would be makes the reveal land hard. This is good sitcom escalation: each beat adds a layer.

jokes.text: Rachel: 'I got to tell you...this really does put me in a better mood.'
jokes.setup: All three women are now in wedding dresses
jokes.punchline: Rachel's sincere report that wearing a wedding dress genuinely improves her emotional state — the honesty is both funny and revealing
jokes.explanation: Rachel's sincere endorsement of the dress-as-therapy is a good character beat. It works because she's not joking — the dress genuinely helps, which is both funny and sad.

jokes.text: Monica: 'I wish there was a job where I could wear this all the time.' Phoebe: 'Maybe someday there will be.'
jokes.setup: Monica expresses the wish that she could wear a wedding dress professionally
jokes.punchline: Phoebe's earnest, optimistic 'Maybe someday there will be' — she treats Monica's impossible wish as a reasonable career goal
jokes.explanation: Phoebe's sunny encouragement of Monica's absurd wish is a perfect Phoebe line — she doesn't question the premise, she just offers hope. The specificity of 'maybe someday there will be' (treating it as a realistic future career) is the joke.

jokes.text: Chandler arrives to borrow candles; Rachel tries to hide them from him: 'Rachel, don't get it! He'll see us!' Rachel: 'The groom cannot see the bride.' Monica: 'I'm not going to marry Chandler.' Rachel: 'Not after this!'
jokes.setup: Chandler knocks; Monica panics that the 'groom' cannot see the 'bride'
jokes.punchline: 'Not after this!' — Rachel's addendum implies she's seen something (presumably Chandler's sad attempt at romance) that disqualifies him as a husband; it's both a joke about their friendship and Chandler's romantic standing
jokes.explanation: The 'not after this' button is excellent — it takes Monica's reasonable denial ('I'm not going to marry Chandler') and extends it with a specific put-down that also implies something about Chandler's character. The irony is rich for rewatch audiences who know Monica and Chandler end up together.

jokes.text: Chandler sees all three women in wedding dresses and simply says 'I do!'
jokes.setup: Chandler enters to find all three women in wedding dresses
jokes.punchline: 'I do!' — he immediately proposes/accepts, treating the sight as a wedding he's being invited to participate in
jokes.explanation: Two words, perfect construction. Chandler's 'I do!' works on multiple levels: it's a natural response to seeing three brides, it's perfectly in character (a quip is his default response to any situation), and for rewatch audiences who know he marries Monica, it's a beautiful piece of dramatic irony. One of the episode's best single-line jokes. The economy is exceptional.

jokes.text: Tag scene: Chandler and Marjorie having a date — she talks in her sleep, he can't sleep because of it. 'Food's here. Fair enough.' ... 'Fifteen-minute warning. Late.'
jokes.setup: Chandler was charmed by Marjorie's sleep-talking and asked her out; now they're on a date
jokes.punchline: She's apparently sleep-talking through the date — narrating/announcing random things ('Food's here. Fair enough. Fifteen-minute warning. Late.') while seemingly awake or barely awake
jokes.explanation: A satisfying callback payoff to the sleep clinic subplot. Chandler's pickup line ('I listen in my sleep') has now created a problem: the girl actually talks in her sleep constantly, and he's stuck with it. The specific fragments of her sleep-talk ('Fair enough,' 'Fifteen-minute warning') are funnier than a generic description would be. Good escalation and callback structure.

jokes.text: Joey, in bed with the mask on, to Chandler: 'Dude, I am trying to sleep!'
jokes.setup: Chandler has apparently come home late/made noise after the disastrous date with Marjorie
jokes.punchline: Joey — who started the entire subplot by keeping Chandler awake with snoring — is now the one demanding quiet, wearing his sleep mask; the reversal is complete
jokes.explanation: A perfect structural callback to close the snoring subplot. The episode opened with Chandler woken by Joey's snoring; it closes with Joey demanding Chandler be quiet so he can sleep. The reversal is satisfying, character-true, and the mask presumably makes it visual. Good closing button.

tmdb_overview: Chandler takes Joey to a sleep clinic when he starts snoring. After Ross asks Monica to pick up Emily's wedding dress, she tries it on and can't stop wearing it. Meanwhile, jealous of Ross's proposal to Emily, Rachel tries to talk Joshua into marriage.
insight: Wedding prep chaos yields 36 jokes, but emotional stakes dilute the comedic payoff.
